extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations (including PR practitioners, association and labor communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and evaluative criteria from a public relations textbook chapter on labor/associations and the role of PR — useful for producing and assessing PR outputs (news releases, newsletters, PSAs) and programs. Focuses on audiences, messages, media, research, evaluation, ethics, and adaptability to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations is increasingly involved in identifying new target audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use research and audience analysis to discover who to reach (demographics, geographics, membership, attentive/aware/active publics) and tailor messages and channels accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing and maintaining key relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing and maintaining key relationships is a core role of public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain relationships through consistent communication, listening, and mutually beneficial interactions; internal and external relationship management (e.g., management–labor relations) is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refining messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations is involved in refining messages to tell the organization’s story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply message framing, priming, connotative/denotative meaning checks, and ensure message content aligns with organizational goals; consider clarity, definiteness, consistency, and distinction when crafting text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building trust / credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Building trust is an explicit function of public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credibility and honesty are essential; use accurate information, transparent practices, and consistent messaging to foster public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of research in public affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs management teams are now using research along with social media and traditional tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate formative and monitoring research methods (surveys, focus groups, content analysis, tracking) to inform strategy, message design, channel selection, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of new media and social media tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Globalization and new media technologies force unions/organizations to better utilize public relations, including social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine social media with traditional tactics; adapt message format and timing for online platforms and monitor online conversations (bloggers, citizen journalists, social networks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of traditional PR tools (news releases, newsletters, PSAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs teams use traditional tools such as news releases, upgraded newsletters, and public service announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate mix (controlled vs. uncontrolled media) depending on audience, message, reach goals, and media relations strategy; ensure each tool meets clarity and accuracy standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability to change
rubrics_metrics.description: Change drives the public relations management function in all organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should be flexible and responsive to environmental, organizational, and media changes; plan for reinvention and experimentation to meet emerging needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable results and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurable results and measurement (measurement, monitoring, evaluation) are central to program assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set key performance indicators (KPIs), benchmarks, and controls; use monitoring, implementation evaluation, and impact evaluation to determine program utility and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact evaluation (knowledge, attitude, behavior outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact evaluation should assess knowledge outcomes, attitude outcomes, and behavioral outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluations to measure intermediate and ultimate impacts (knowledge gain, attitude change, behavior change); use impact criteria and methods and track key results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message dissemination, distribution, and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Message dissemination and distribution (message placement, message dissemination) are important program functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan distribution to maximize reach and placement effectiveness (media placement, timing, targeted outlets); monitor dissemination success and adapt placement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channels of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Channels of communication (channels, mediums) are key considerations for PR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose among broadcast, print, internet, intranets, controlled media, and face-to-face channels based on audience capability, involvement, and message goals; coordinate channels for integrated campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reach and capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience reach and capability are metrics to consider when planning and evaluating communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential audience size (reach) and the audience’s capability to receive/process messages (literacy, involvement) to set realistic objectives and choose channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and the Seven Cs of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication quality includes clarity and the seven Cs (clear, concise, concrete, correct, coherent, complete, courteous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the seven Cs as a checklist when drafting releases and other materials; ensure messages are definite, consistent, and understandable to target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy of information is a fundamental standard in public relations practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts and sources before release; accuracy underpins credibility and helps avoid legal/ethical problems (libel, false light, defamation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability metrics (Fog Index, Gunning Formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readability formulas such as the Fog Index and Gunning Formula are cited for assessing written communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use readability measures to calibrate sentence length, vocabulary, and complexity so materials match audience reading level and improve comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message framing and priming
rubrics_metrics.description: Message framing and cognitive priming are tools for shaping how audiences interpret information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame messages strategically (emphasis, metaphors, semantics) and use priming techniques thoughtfully to influence salience and perception; avoid manipulative or dishonest framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and working with media
rubrics_metrics.description: Media relations (working with media, media strategy) are core activities in PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop relationships with journalists and outlets, understand media norms, prepare clear press materials (news releases, backgrounders), and plan media strategies for crises and campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation and timing (crisis anticipation, disasters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipating crises and disasters and timing responses are highlighted as PR responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have plans for emerging and immediate crises, anticipate issues, prepare information centers/hotlines, and time releases appropriately to manage public perception and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and ethical constraints (libel, copyright, First Amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal considerations include libel/defamation, copyright/trademark, First Amendment rights, lobbying laws, and labor relations statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure releases and campaigns comply with applicable laws (copyright, libel, lobbying disclosure) and professional codes of ethics; consult legal counsel when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key performance indicators and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Key performance indicators (KPIs) and benchmark evaluation models are part of evaluating PR program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define KPIs tied to goals (awareness, attitude, behavior, media placements), use benchmarking to compare progress over time or against standards, and adjust tactics based on monitoring data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience segmentation by public types (latent/aware/active/hot-issue publics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment target publics into types (latent, aware, active, hot-issue, all-issue publics) to guide strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor messages and tactics to the public’s level of awareness, involvement, and issue salience; prioritize active and hot-issue publics for mobilization efforts.
